summary: ERC-8004 moves no money and checks no identities, so most payment rules land on the rails and wallets used next to it, not on the registry. The registry-specific issues are data protection (permanent public records), the absence of KYC or know-your-agent, and reliance on contracts one key can upgrade. ERC-8226 (Draft) is the only standard found that adds a compliance and mandate layer for regulated tokens. Rows are dated; check the source before relying on any of them.

rows.text: The registries hold and move no funds, so money transmission rules do not reach the registry itself. FinCEN guidance FIN-2019-G001 applies to businesses that transmit value, such as the payment rail an agent uses alongside ERC-8004.

ERC-8004 has no KYC or know-your-agent check. OFAC sanctions obligations apply the same way to digital and fiat transactions, so screening of an agentWallet address falls to whoever sends the payment.

The GENIUS Act (signed 2025-07-18) regulates payment stablecoin issuers; it applies to payments made to an agentWallet in stablecoins, not to the registry. Final rules were still pending on 2026-10-11.

Regulation E and Regulation Z decide unauthorized-use liability for account and card payments; an ERC-8004 identity or reputation score does not change that allocation, and no CFPB rule on AI agents was found.
California's ADMT regulations (effective 2026-01-01) can apply to a business that uses automated scoring of people; public reputation data about agents may still describe their operators.
GDPR covers any information relating to an identifiable person. Feedback events, hashes and URIs cannot be deleted from the chain, which conflicts with erasure if personal data is placed there.
AI Act Article 50 transparency duties apply from 2026-08-02; an agent discovered through ERC-8004 that talks to people must still disclose it is an AI. The registry adds no AI Act duty of its own.
MiCA governs e-money tokens and crypto-asset service providers (transition ended 2026-07-01); it applies to the payment rail and wallet providers, not to a registry that moves no assets.
The Transfer of Funds Regulation applies the travel rule to crypto-asset transfers through providers. ERC-8004 feedback files carry only addresses and a transaction hash, not originator data.
PSD2 strong customer authentication applies to payment service providers; ERC-8004 identity is not an authentication factor under it.
UK GDPR as amended by the Data (Use and Access) Act 2025 applies the same erasure concern to personal data placed in permanent on-chain records.
The FCA (2026-03-25) said it will consider whether payments regulation must change for agentic AI; HM Treasury consulted from 2026-07-14 to 2026-10-06. Neither names agent registries.
The Money Laundering Regulations 2017 cover cryptoasset businesses; a registry that moves no assets is outside them, the payment provider is not.
PIPEDA governs private-sector personal information, including any personal data in public feedback files.
The Stablecoin Act in Bill C-15 received Royal Assent on 2026-03-26 and applies to issuers, not to identity registries.

MAS Guidelines on AI Risk Management (issued 2026-10-07, effective 2027-10-07) mention agentic AI for financial institutions that use it; a regulated firm relying on ERC-8004 scores would treat them as a third-party input.
The Personal Data Protection Act 2012 applies to personal data in public records an organization publishes.
No Visa or Mastercard rule refers to ERC-8004. Agent identity in card programs comes from network registration, and no agent-specific liability rule was public on 2026-10-11.
